title: Excel AI assistant for workbooks, tables and .xlsx files
h1: an excel bot for the workbook you actually mean
description: Get budget versus actual before the meeting. Connect a OneDrive workbook or drop an .xlsx into Metal for range, table and chart work.
answer: **get budget versus actual before the board meeting, without hunting through workbook copies.** dusk's excel connection reads and changes ranges, tables and charts. two ways in: a workbook in onedrive, or a file you drop in the chat. say which. name the sheet and where the result belongs. start with a report here before letting the bot write cells.

review.by: lead agent: read against seo/facts, automated gate, independent fact-check pass

og_line: connected workbooks or a file in chat.

app.name: Excel
app.intro:
**choose a connected workbook or attach the file.**

- the excel toolkit uses composio's microsoft excel connection. its workbook actions are separate from local attachments.
- choose a connected workbook for ongoing app work.
- attach the .xlsx when the job concerns that file.

highlight.use: locate a workbook by name before inspecting its contents
confirm which sheets are present in that workbook
find the occupied area of a sheet for review
read budget vs actual for the range you name
inspect the entries in a named workbook table
write the numbers into the cells you named
chart this month against last for the board deck
prepare a pdf version of the workbook for review

app.setup:
**name the file and sheet before asking for an edit.**

for connected work, choose excel in **connected apps** and sign in through microsoft. allow the workbook bot to use it.

for a file task, drop the .xlsx into chat or use **attach files**. say what to inspect and ask for the result as a file in chat. you can also give it a project folder.

routines_intro: **get a useful report before handing over the cells.** name the workbook, sheet and columns. let it write only after a few correct reports.

routines.name: budget variance reading
routines.message: every monday at noon, read the budget and actual columns in the connected planning workbook. list the largest differences with both inputs and each row label. keep currencies separate. change no formulas, values or formatting. if you cannot read a source value, say so.
routines.output: a variance report here, with source values beside each difference

routines.name: staffing table gaps
routines.message: every wednesday at 9, read the allocation table in the connected staffing workbook. flag rows missing a person, week or assigned hours. name the row and missing field. leave entries and table order alone. if every row is complete, say so briefly.
routines.output: a checklist of incomplete entries; the staffing table stays unchanged

routines.name: month-end report copy
routines.message: on the last day of each month at 3, find the connected monthly workbook for that month. show me its sheet names. wait for my confirmation before edits or export. after i confirm, make a pdf here for review. don't email it or reuse last month's file if the current one is missing.
routines.when: last day of the month at 15:00
routines.output: the selected workbook and its pdf report here after your review

asks:
**keep the figures intact while you try the reports.** give the bot read-only excel access. for cell changes later, restrict the action list and write "ask me before you change anything". cell edits use app permissions, so they can happen without a sending prompt.

attached-file work uses the bot's computer permissions instead. start on **ask for approval** while you see how it handles your workbook.
cannot: **edit a connected range with read-only access.** a report here can stay separate from workbook writes.
**react to each workbook edit through this connection.** the excel catalog has no events. schedule the report instead.
**finish local workbook work during sleep.** the app and machine must stay awake. move timed jobs to an always-on bot machine when needed.

sections.md:
**name the source and stop the copy hunt.** for a one-off, say "review this attached workbook and return findings here". for recurring work, name the connected file and sheet.

ask which workbook the bot read. [google sheets](/integrations/google-sheets) uses a different connection, so name that source separately.

**put the report where you will use it.** generated files appear in chat and live in the bot's folder or a project folder you give it.

choose that folder for a [file organisation routine](/use-cases/file-organizer). to email a report later, connect [outlook](/integrations/outlook) separately and review the send there.

faq.q: can i just drop an excel file into the chat?
faq.a: **yes, attach the .xlsx.** describe the job and ask for the result here. giving the bot that file needs no microsoft account connection.

faq.q: is this an excel connection or desktop screen control?
faq.a: **the highlighted tools are app actions.** they use composio's microsoft excel connection. attached-file work is another route. neither promises control of an open excel window.

faq.q: can it watch every workbook edit as it happens?
faq.a: **schedule the report instead.** the excel catalog has no triggers for workbook edits. choose how often you need fresh figures.

tip.text: ask for source values beside the conclusion. a variance without its inputs is harder to trust.
